body.x: LORDSYSTEM (CEO Yangho Jang) will participate in CES 2025, held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, USA, as part of the ‘K-Startup Pavilion.’

LORDSYSTEM offers a passport DID (Decentralized Identifier) authentication solution that enables real-time verification of passport authenticity via mobile devices. The solution compares information on the user’s passport with data stored in its electronic chip and cross-verifies the user’s facial recognition information to generate a secure QR code containing user details. Encrypting personal data with blockchain technology ensures robust security, preventing data leaks and fraudulent use during authentication.

Building on its passport DID platform, LORDSYSTEM operates TripPASS, a mobile platform that allows foreign tourists to access transportation and financial services seamlessly, equivalent to domestic users. The platform also issues prepaid cards and supports services like mobile tax refunds, duty-free identity verification, and casino entry authentication for foreigners, with plans to expand its applications further.

At CES 2025, LORDSYSTEM will introduce its non-face-to-face authentication platform, LORDPASS. This platform separates TripPASS's eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer) functions to create a scalable system. LORDPASS leverages blockchain technology to verify user data in real time, serving as a gateway for membership registration, payments, and broader foreign market expansion.

LORDSYSTEM has been actively building partnerships, including with Japan’s DNP (Dai Nippon Printing Co., Ltd), and is a founding member of the Asia-Pacific Digital Identity Consortium (APDI). APDI aims to standardize and enhance interoperability for digital identity solutions across the Asia-Pacific region, with plans for a mobile authentication proof-of-concept (POC) by late 2025.

The company expressed its ambition to identify global partners at CES 2025 to expand passport application further DID authentication and eKYC solutions, emphasizing its commitment to innovation and cross-border digital identity initiatives.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally.
